  "id": "ALE-440",
  "uuid": "31c734d0-d03b-4fb1-89ab-0c041a6bc19b",
  "title": "Regular Workshops: manual destinations and attendee directions",
  "description": "## Parent\n\n<issue id=\"98030fc2-d822-4d02-90e8-305aec1a8396\" label=\"ALE-438\" href=\"https://linear.app/alessandrojcm/issue/ALE-438/spec-workshop-venue-autocomplete-and-directions\" /> — Spec: Workshop venue autocomplete and directions.\n\n## What to build\n\nA coordinator can add a manually entered destination to a new or ordinarily editable regular Workshop, and members and external attendees can use it for directions on their existing workshop pages. Both Calendar audiences receive the recognizable destination through the existing native location field. Deliver this without requiring Google Places configuration.\n\nPublishing this ticket specifies later work; it does not start implementation or authorize Google provisioning, billing/key changes, production activation or production backfill. Obtain implementation authorization before code changes, and separate operational authorization before any live Google or production work.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Keep the required short venue label separate from nullable manual destination details and an optional manual Maps link. Add compatible storage and request/read contracts so existing rows and label-only submissions remain valid. Do not introduce Google-derived persistence in this slice.\n- [ ] Introduce a domain-neutral destination input composed from the existing UI primitives and use it in regular Workshop create/edit. Preserve remote-form-derived control names, values and field errors after rejection, keyboard access and usable phone layout. The input must be reusable by Beginners' Workshops without importing Workshop policy.\n- [ ] Persist and read back manually entered destinations through the ordinary public Workshop operations. Omitted destination fields preserve existing data, explicit clear removes optional details, and unrelated edits do not lose directions. Keep authorization and planned-only general editing intact; the published pricing exception does not permit venue edits.\n- [ ] Validate optional manual URLs server-side as supported HTTPS Maps destinations. Reject executable schemes, credentials and unsupported targets through the existing problem/field-error seam. A manual name/address remains useful without requiring a link or a provider listing.\n- [ ] Show the familiar label, useful destination details and safe external directions links on existing member and external attendee surfaces. Legacy rows retain their label without fabricating a selected Place from unreviewed text. Add no embedded map, location-permission prompt or new public listing.\n- [ ] Extend the source-owned Calendar projection with recognizable destination name/address and label fallback. Reuse the existing synchronization protocol for committee and participant events; participant descriptions stay absent and the committee description retains only its protected dashboard link.\n- [ ] Record identifier-only Calendar intent atomically with a destination change. Keep Google outside source transactions, preserve existing event identity and surviving RSVPs, use normal participant update notifications for meaningful changes, keep committee mutations non-notifying and unchanged reconciliation silent. Deployment does not activate sending.\n- [ ] Exercise actual create/edit submissions through the existing browser and E2E journeys, public source operations, attendee-safe reads, controller contracts and generated client. Cover manual-only and optional-link entry, rejection recovery, unsafe URLs, omission/clear, unrelated edits and legacy data.\n- [ ] Run the existing Calendar sync boundary with Req.Test Google/OAuth substitution after real source writes. Assert native location for both audiences, privacy, notification parameters and no duplicate event or extra update on a no-op. Existing email templates, booking, payment and refund rules remain unchanged.\n\n## Blocked by\n\nNone — can start immediately.\n\n>>> Agent notes\n\nUse ADR 0003's OpenAPI-first workflow and regenerate the typed client. Complete affected frontend build, typecheck, lint, unit/browser/E2E checks, Phoenix precommit and API generation/idempotency checks; review changed browser baselines and rerun without update mode. Use public source operations and the existing Calendar sync seam, not mocked internal helpers. This ticket intentionally does not relax the published editor or implement reviewed backfill.\n\n>>>",

Do not introduce Google-derived persistence in this slice.\n- [ ] Introduce a domain-neutral destination input composed from the existing UI primitives and use it in regular Workshop create/edit. Preserve remote-form-derived control names, values and field errors after rejection, keyboard access and usable phone layout. Keep Google outside source transactions, preserve existing event identity and surviving RSVPs, use normal participant update notifications for meaningful changes, keep committee mutations non-notifying and unchanged reconciliation silent. Deployment does not activate sending.\n- [ ] Exercise actual create/edit submissions through the existing browser and E2E journeys, public source operations, attendee-safe reads, controller contracts and generated client. Stub Stripe HTTP with `Dhc.StripeHTTPStub` (`stub/3`, `expect/4`, `form/1`, `json/3`) — no Bypass, and tests never `put_env` `:stripe_api_url`, `:stripe_secret_key` or `:stripe_req_options`. Stubs reach Tasks/inline jobs via `$callers`; other processes need `Req.Test.allow/3`. Shared subscription-payment decoding lives in `Dhc.Stripe.SubscriptionPayment` and the one retry rule in `Dhc.Stripe.Failure.retryable?/1`; see "Stubbing Stripe" in `docs/agents/notes.md`.

- Use the already included and available `:req` (`Req`) library for HTTP requests, **avoid** `:httpoison`, `:tesla`, and `:httpc`. Req is included by default and is the preferred HTTP client for Phoenix apps
- **Documented exception (ADR 0021)**: transactional email goes through Swoosh, whose api client is `config :swoosh, api_client: Dhc.Email.ApiClient` wrapping `Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch` over a named `{Finch, name: Swoosh.Finch}` child in `Dhc.Application`. ### Phoenix v1.8 guidelines

- **Always** begin your LiveView templates with `<Layouts.app flash={@flash} ...>` which wraps all inner content
- The `MyAppWeb.Layouts` module is aliased in the `my_app_web.ex` file, so you can use it without needing to alias it again
- Anytime you run into errors with no `current_scope` assign:
  - You failed to follow the Authenticated Routes guidelines, or you failed to pass `current_scope` to `<Layouts.app>`
  - **Always** fix the `current_scope` error by moving your routes to the proper `live_session` and ensure you pass `current_scope` as needed

- Out of the box, `core_components.ex` imports an `<.icon name="hero-x-mark" class="w-5 h-5"/>` component for hero icons. **Always** use the `<.icon>` component for icons, **never** use `Heroicons` modules or similar
- **Always** use the imported `<.input>` component for form inputs from `core_components.ex` when available. `<.input>` is imported and using it will save steps and prevent errors
- If you override the default input classes (`<.input class="myclass px-2 py-1 rounded-lg">)`) class with your own values, no default classes are inherited, so your
custom classes must fully style the input


<!-- usage-rules-start -->

<!-- phoenix:elixir-start -->
## Elixir guidelines

- Elixir lists **do not support index based access via the access syntax**

  **Never do this (invalid)**:

      i = 0
      mylist = ["blue", "green"]
      mylist[i]

  Instead, **always** use `Enum.at`, pattern matching, or `List` for index based list access, ie:

      i = 0
      mylist = ["blue", "green"]
      Enum.at(mylist, i)

- Elixir variables are immutable, but can be rebound, so for block expressions like `if`, `case`, `cond`, etc
  you *must* bind the result of the expression to a variable if you want to use it and you CANNOT rebind the result inside the expression, ie:

      # INVALID: we are rebinding inside the `if` and the result never gets assigned
      if connected?(socket) do
        socket = assign(socket, :val, val)
      end

      # VALID: we rebind the result of the `if` to a new variable
      socket =
        if connected?(socket) do
          assign(socket, :val, val)
        end

- **Never** nest multiple modules in the same file as it can cause cyclic dependencies and compilation errors
- **Never** use map access syntax (`changeset[:field]`) on structs as they do not implement the Access behaviour by default. For regular structs, you **must** access the fields directly, such as `my_struct.field` or use higher level APIs that are available on the struct if they exist, `Ecto.Changeset.get_field/2` for changesets
- Elixir's standard library has everything necessary for date and time manipulation. Familiarize yourself with the common `Time`, `Date`, `DateTime`, and `Calendar` interfaces by accessing their documentation as necessary. The one sanctioned date/time dependency is `tz`, the IANA database behind `Dhc.ClubCalendar`'s Europe/Dublin conversions. **Never** install additional dependencies unless asked or for date/time parsing (which you can use the `date_time_parser` package)
- Don't use `String.to_atom/1` on user input (memory leak risk)
- Predicate function names should not start with `is_` and should end in a question mark. Names like `is_thing` should be reserved for guards
- Elixir's builtin OTP primitives like `DynamicSupervisor` and `Registry`, require names in the child spec, such as `{DynamicSupervisor, name: MyApp.MyDynamicSup}`, then you can use `DynamicSupervisor.start_child(MyApp.MyDynamicSup, child_spec)`
- Use `Task.async_stream(collection, callback, options)` for concurrent enumeration with back-pressure. The majority of times you will want to pass `timeout: :infinity` as option

## Mix guidelines

- Read the docs and options before using tasks (by using `mix help task_name`)
- To debug test failures, run tests in a specific file with `mix test test/my_test.exs` or run all previously failed tests with `mix test --failed`
- `mix deps.clean --all` is **almost never needed**. **Avoid** using it unless you have good reason

## Test guidelines

- **Always use `start_supervised!/1`** to start processes in tests as it guarantees cleanup between tests
- **Avoid** `Process.sleep/1` and `Process.alive?/1` in tests
  - Instead of sleeping to wait for a process to finish, **always** use `Process.monitor/1` and assert on the DOWN message:

      ref = Process.monitor(pid)
      assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, :normal}

   - Instead of sleeping to synchronize before the next call, **always** use `_ = :sys.get_state/1` to ensure the process has handled prior messages
<!-- phoenix:elixir-end -->

<!-- phoenix:phoenix-start -->
## Phoenix guidelines

- Remember Phoenix router `scope` blocks include an optional alias which is prefixed for all routes within the scope. **Always** be mindful of this when creating routes within a scope to avoid duplicate module prefixes.

- You **never** need to create your own `alias` for route definitions! The `scope` provides the alias, ie:

      scope "/admin", AppWeb.Admin do
        pipe_through :browser

        live "/users", UserLive, :index
      end

  the UserLive route would point to the `AppWeb.Admin.UserLive` module

- `Phoenix.View` no longer is needed or included with Phoenix, don't use it
<!-- phoenix:phoenix-end -->

<!-- phoenix:ecto-start -->
## Ecto Guidelines

- **Always** preload Ecto associations in queries when they'll be accessed in templates, ie a message that needs to reference the `message.user.email`
- Remember `import Ecto.Query` and other supporting modules when you write `seeds.exs`
- `Ecto.Schema` fields always use the `:string` type, even for `:text`, columns, ie: `field :name, :string`
- `Ecto.Changeset.validate_number/2` **DOES NOT SUPPORT the `:allow_nil` option**. By default, Ecto validations only run if a change for the given field exists and the change value is not nil, so such as option is never needed
- You **must** use `Ecto.Changeset.get_field(changeset, :field)` to access changeset fields
- Fields which are set programmatically, such as `user_id`, must not be listed in `cast` calls or similar for security purposes. Instead they must be explicitly set when creating the struct
- **Always** invoke `mix ecto.gen.migration migration_name_using_underscores` when generating migration files, so the correct timestamp and conventions are applied
<!-- phoenix:ecto-end -->

<!-- usage-rules-end -->

- Elixir's standard library has everything necessary for date and time manipulation. Familiarize yourself with the common `Time`, `Date`, `DateTime`, and `Calendar` interfaces by accessing their documentation as necessary. The one sanctioned date/time dependency is `tz`, the IANA database behind `Dhc.ClubCalendar`'s Europe/Dublin conversions. **Never** install additional dependencies unless asked or for date/time parsing (which you can use the `date_time_parser` package)
- Don't use `String.to_atom/1` on user input (memory leak risk)
- Predicate function names should not start with `is_` and should end in a question mark. Names like `is_thing` should be reserved for guards
- Elixir's builtin OTP primitives like `DynamicSupervisor` and `Registry`, require names in the child spec, such as `{DynamicSupervisor, name: MyApp.MyDynamicSup}`, then you can use `DynamicSupervisor.start_child(MyApp.MyDynamicSup, child_spec)`
- Use `Task.async_stream(collection, callback, options)` for concurrent enumeration with back-pressure. The majority of times you will want to pass `timeout: :infinity` as option

## Mix guidelines

- Read the docs and options before using tasks (by using `mix help task_name`)
- To debug test failures, run tests in a specific file with `mix test test/my_test.exs` or run all previously failed tests with `mix test --failed`
- `mix deps.clean --all` is **almost never needed**. **Avoid** using it unless you have good reason

## Test guidelines

- **Always use `start_supervised!/1`** to start processes in tests as it guarantees cleanup between tests
- **Avoid** `Process.sleep/1` and `Process.alive?/1` in tests
  - Instead of sleeping to wait for a process to finish, **always** use `Process.monitor/1` and assert on the DOWN message:

      ref = Process.monitor(pid)
      assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, :normal}

   - Instead of sleeping to synchronize before the next call, **always** use `_ = :sys.get_state/1` to ensure the process has handled prior messages
<!-- phoenix:elixir-end -->

<!-- phoenix:phoenix-start -->
## Phoenix guidelines

- Remember Phoenix router `scope` blocks include an optional alias which is prefixed for all routes within the scope. **Always** be mindful of this when creating routes within a scope to avoid duplicate module prefixes.

- You **never** need to create your own `alias` for route definitions! The `scope` provides the alias, ie:

      scope "/admin", AppWeb.Admin do
        pipe_through :browser

        live "/users", UserLive, :index
      end

  the UserLive route would point to the `AppWeb.Admin.UserLive` module

- `Phoenix.View` no longer is needed or included with Phoenix, don't use it
<!-- phoenix:phoenix-end -->

<!-- phoenix:ecto-start -->
## Ecto Guidelines

- **Always** preload Ecto associations in queries when they'll be accessed in templates, ie a message that needs to reference the `message.user.email`
- Remember `import Ecto.Query` and other supporting modules when you write `seeds.exs`
- `Ecto.Schema` fields always use the `:string` type, even for `:text`, columns, ie: `field :name, :string`
- `Ecto.Changeset.validate_number/2` **DOES NOT SUPPORT the `:allow_nil` option**. By default, Ecto validations only run if a change for the given field exists and the change value is not nil, so such as option is never needed
- You **must** use `Ecto.Changeset.get_field(changeset, :field)` to access changeset fields
- Fields which are set programmatically, such as `user_id`, must not be listed in `cast` calls or similar for security purposes. Instead they must be explicitly set when creating the struct
- **Always** invoke `mix ecto.gen.migration migration_name_using_underscores` when generating migration files, so the correct timestamp and conventions are applied
<!-- phoenix:ecto-end -->

content.text: **Summarizing test results and assumptions**

Implemented ALE-441 frontend.

- Added destination fields to Beginners’ Workshop schedule/reschedule forms.
- Added separate “Destination” enrichment dialog using `beginnersWorkshopsEnrichDestination`, so destination edits do not use rescheduling.
- Extended shared destination input with persisted-value prefills.
- Rendered destination details and no-referrer directions link on the public Intake page.
- Added browser coverage for schedule field names, reschedule compatibility, Intake directions, and enrichment dialog.

Verified:
- `pnpm --filter @dhc/web check`
- `pnpm --filter @dhc/web build`
- Focused browser tests: 28 passing
- Focused Oxlint: passing

Assumption confirmed against concurrent contract work: API operation is `beginnersWorkshops.enrichDestination`, generated as `beginnersWorkshopsEnrichDestination`; destination fields live on `BeginnersIntakeWorkshop`.

Not changed: Phoenix/backend or generated-client files. Existing Svelte warnings and Vitest hanging-process shutdown warnings remain unrelated.
